## Description

When `partio enable` runs, register hooks in the agent's native hook configuration (for Claude Code: `.claude/settings.local.json`) alongside the existing git hooks. This gives Partio explicit session lifecycle signals (`SessionStart` and `Stop`) rather than relying solely on process detection at commit time, and matches the timeout pattern introduced in the source product.

Source: [entireio/cli#1237](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1237) — add timeout to session-start hook; [entireio/cli#1065](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/1065) — CLI hangs blocking agent hooks; [entireio/cli#957](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/957)/[#1072](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/1072) — repeated hook timeouts.

## What to build

1. Add a Claude Code hook installer that reads and writes `.claude/settings.local.json` in the repo root. The installer must:
   - Add a `SessionStart` entry invoking `partio _hook claude-code session-start` with a `timeout` of 10 (a number of seconds).
   - Add a `Stop` entry invoking `partio _hook claude-code session-stop` with a `timeout` of 10 (a number of seconds).
   - Be idempotent: skip entries that are already present.
   - Preserve all existing user-defined entries in the file.
   - Handle a missing file by creating it with `{"hooks": {}}` (`hooks` is an object keyed by event name).
2. Extend `cmd/partio/enable.go` to call the Claude Code hook installer when the configured agent is `claude-code` (the default).
3. Extend `cmd/partio/hook.go` to route the two-argument form `partio _hook claude-code session-start` and `partio _hook claude-code session-stop` to handlers (the handlers may be no-ops initially but must not return an error).
4. Extend `cmd/partio/disable.go` to remove only the Partio-managed entries from `.claude/settings.local.json` (identified by the `partio _hook` command string), leaving user-defined entries intact.
5. Extend `cmd/partio/doctor.go` to check that the Claude Code `SessionStart` and `Stop` hook entries exist in `.claude/settings.local.json` and that the `partio` binary they reference is reachable.

**Notes (argos review, 2026-10-10).** The target file is `.claude/settings.local.json`, not `.claude/settings.json`: `settings.json` is shared through git (this repository tracks one), so a teammate without `partio` would get a failing hook in each session, while Partio's git hooks are per clone. Format (checked in a local Claude Code settings file): `hooks` is an object keyed by event name; each event holds an array of `{"matcher": …, "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "…", "timeout": 10}]}`, and `timeout` is a number of seconds. Design call: Partio has no agent-native hooks today, and these handlers stay no-ops until a feature uses them (for example #455).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `partio enable` (with `claude-code` as the configured agent) writes `SessionStart` and `Stop` hook entries into `.claude/settings.local.json`
- [ ] Each installed entry includes a `timeout` field set to 10 seconds
- [ ] Running `partio enable` twice does not duplicate hook entries in `.claude/settings.local.json`
- [ ] Existing user-defined entries in `.claude/settings.local.json` are preserved after `partio enable` and `partio disable`
- [ ] `partio disable` removes the Partio-managed hook entries from `.claude/settings.local.json`
- [ ] `partio _hook claude-code session-start` and `partio _hook claude-code session-stop` are accepted without returning "unknown hook"
- [ ] `partio doctor` reports whether the Claude Code agent-native hooks are registered and valid

## Premise

<!-- partio:premise:v1 -->

- Partio detects agent sessions via process detection at git commit time and not via agent-native lifecycle events [evidence: `internal/agent/claude/process.go`]
- `partio enable` installs only git hooks and does not write to `.claude/settings.local.json` [evidence: `cmd/partio/enable.go`]
- `partio _hook` accepts only `pre-commit`, `post-commit`, and `pre-push`; any other name returns an error [evidence: `cmd/partio/hook.go`]
- `partio disable` removes only git hooks and does not modify agent-native config files [evidence: `cmd/partio/disable.go`]
- `partio doctor` checks only git hooks, the checkpoint branch, and binary presence in PATH [evidence: `cmd/partio/doctor.go`]

## Gathered Evidence

**Claim 1**: Partio detects agent sessions via process detection at git commit time and not via agent-native lifecycle events.
- Evidence: `internal/agent/claude/process.go` — `IsRunning()` calls `exec.Command("pgrep", "-f", "claude").Output()` with no timeout or context. `internal/agent/pgrep.go` — `PgrepFirst()` likewise. No integration with `.claude/settings.local.json` or agent-native hook events anywhere in `internal/agent/`.
- Verdict: holds.

**Claim 2**: `partio enable` installs only git hooks and does not write to `.claude/settings.local.json`.
- Evidence: `cmd/partio/enable.go` — `runEnable` calls `githooks.Install(repoRoot)` for the three git hooks and writes `.partio/settings.json`. The only flags are `--absolute-path`; there is no `--agent` flag. No file path containing `.claude` appears in this file or in `internal/git/hooks/`.
- Verdict: holds.

**Claim 3**: `partio _hook` accepts only `pre-commit`, `post-commit`, and `pre-push`; any other name returns an error.
- Evidence: `cmd/partio/hook.go` lines 36–45 — `switch hookName` routes exactly these three names; the `default` branch returns `fmt.Errorf("unknown hook: %s", hookName)`.
- Verdict: holds.

**Claim 4**: `partio disable` removes only git hooks and does not modify agent-native config files.
- Evidence: `cmd/partio/disable.go` — no reference to `claude`, `settings`, or agent config paths. Only calls `githooks.Uninstall()`.
- Verdict: holds.

**Claim 5**: `partio doctor` checks only git hooks, the checkpoint branch, and binary presence in PATH.
- Evidence: `cmd/partio/doctor.go` — no reference to `claude`, `settings`, or agent config paths. Checks: `.partio/` directory, three git hooks, checkpoint branch, binary in PATH.
- Verdict: holds.

Proposal id: register-agent-native-lifecycle-hooks-during-enable
